title: Cabernet Franc in Bordeaux
subtitle: A blending partner
objectives: Explain Cabernet Franc's role in Bordeaux blends
Name Bordeaux wines with high Cabernet Franc
Explain why it suits the Right Bank

steps.title: A supporting role
steps.body: In Bordeaux, Cabernet Franc is about 10% of red plantings. It adds aromatic lift, freshness and fine tannins to blends. On the Left Bank, it's a minor partner to Cabernet Sauvignon. On the Right Bank, in Saint-Émilion and Pomerol, it often plays a bigger role alongside Merlot.

steps.title: Cheval Blanc and Ausone
steps.body: Château Cheval Blanc, in Saint-Émilion, often uses over 50% Cabernet Franc, on gravel and clay near Pomerol. Château Ausone, on limestone slopes, also uses around half. These show Cabernet Franc can make some of the world's greatest wines, with perfume, freshness and longevity.
steps.highlight: Cheval Blanc: over half Cabernet Franc

steps.prompt: Which Saint-Émilion estate often uses over 50% Cabernet Franc?
steps.explanation: Cheval Blanc is famous for its high share of Cabernet Franc.

steps.title: Why the Right Bank
steps.body: The Right Bank's cooler clay and limestone suit early-ripening grapes. Cabernet Franc ripens before Cabernet Sauvignon, so it does well there. Limestone slopes give it freshness and structure, complementing Merlot's plumpness.

steps.prompt: Cabernet Franc is the most planted grape in Bordeaux.
steps.explanation: Not true. Merlot is the most planted. Cabernet Franc is about 10%.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cabernet Franc adds lift and freshness to Bordeaux blends
Cheval Blanc and Ausone use a high share
It suits the Right Bank's cooler soils
